To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
atherogenic dysplipidemia is associated with increased CV risk, and that fenofibrate-stain combinations can be used to reduce this risk.
the combination of fenofibrate with statins is an effective and well-tolerated treatment for patients with athero-genic dyslipidaemia.
atherogenic dysliplipidaemia (AD) is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD), and that fenofibrate-stain combination therapy can reduce CVD risk in patients with AD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of fenfo-bibrate-statin combination in patients with AD.
the use of fenofibrate in patients with AD and elevated triglycerides, with or without low HDL-c levels, who are at risk of CV events despite treatment with statin therapy.
the development of new methods for measuring and controlling blood lipids, and in particular, the development of new therapies for the treatment of hyperlipidaemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fenofibrate-stain combination therapy is recommended for patients with AD and elevated triglyceride plus low HDL-c levels, to help achieve target levels of non-HDL cholesterol.

the combination of a statin with fenofibrate should be considered for patients at high CV risk who have atherogenic dyslpidemia, and that non-HDL-c is a more appropriate target than LDL-c for CV risk management in these patients.

the combination of statin and fibrate therapy should be considered in high CV risk patients with atherogenically dyslipidaemic profile, and in those with atherogenic lipoprotein profile, in whom the LDL-c goal has been achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination therapy of a fenofibrate with a statin in patients with elevated triglyceride plus low HDL-c levels is recommended, as this is the best way to reduce the residual CV risk in patients with AD.
fenofibrate-stain combination therapy is an effective and safe option for the management of AD and CV risk reduction in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and/or metabolic syndrome.
the combination of statin and fenofibrate therapy in patients with AD is safe, well-tolerated and effective in reducing the CV risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to statin therapy for patients with AD and elevated CV risk, fenofibrate should be added to further improve the lipid profile and to reduce the risk of CV disease.

the combination of fenofibrate with a statin should be considered in patients who have elevated trigyceride and/or low levels of HDH-c despite treatment with a statin, to help achieve target non-HDL cholesterol levels and to reduce CV risk.
a combination therapy with a statin plus fenofibrate is recommended for the treatment of AD, and that non-HDL-c should be used to guide therapy.
